title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 40-42): Grothendieck is building automorphisms u of an S_0-group scheme 𝔊^+. 𝔊^+ is an extension of a small discrete group by an abelian group scheme M. That discrete group is generated by ρ and σ, with ω = σ^2 central, which looks like SL_2(Z)-type data for the modular / genus-0 and genus-1 tower. The automorphisms are parametrized by points of the smooth scheme Σ̃_{ρ,σ} introduced on p. 40. A point of Σ̃ is (ν, ν', ν_2, ν_3, α_0, β_0) with ν = 2ν' + ν_2, 2ν+1 invertible, and α_0, β_0 sections of M subject to the 'loop equation' (32): (1-ρ)α_0 = (1-σ)β_0 + (ν - ν_3)λ_1.

On this page:
- Σ̃ is given a natural group structure and is made to act on 𝔊^+ by (33)/(36): u(ρ) = ξ·ρ and u(σ) = ω^{ν_2}·η_0·σ, where ξ = α_0 - ρ(α_0) + ν_3λ_1 and η_0 = β_0 - σ(β_0) are sections of M (35). The '+' in the second line of (33) is a slip for a product.
- He notes that one must check u respects the defining relations of 𝔊^+, chiefly relation (7)/(34), [σ, λ_∞].
- To do this he computes u on the generators of M: λ_0 = ω l_0 = ω σρσρ and λ_1 = ω l_1 = ω ρσρσ.
- The 'loop relation' gives u(ε_0) = ε_0^{(μ)}, with μ = 2ν+1 = 4ν' + 2ν_2 + 1.
- The next page concludes u(ω) = ω and u(λ) = μ·λ on M. So u acts on the abelian kernel through the 'cyclotomic' scalar μ, and on the generators by twisted conjugation by cocycle-like elements ξ, η_0.

In modern terms, this is a metabelian (abelian-kernel) truncation of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type parametrization. An automorphism is (λ = 2m+1, f), with u(x) = conjugate of x^λ, u(y) = f^{-1} y^λ f. It must preserve the inertia ('lacets') conjugacy classes and the relations of the modular-type group. The parity bookkeeping μ = 2ν+1, ν = 2ν' + ν_2 parallels Drinfeld's λ = 2m+1 in the 2-cycle relation. Grothendieck works scheme-theoretically over S_0 (char 2 and 3 are flagged on p. 40). The purpose is to show that the parameter scheme Σ̃ acts as a smooth group scheme of automorphisms, as a model for the Galois/Teichmüller action at the first nonabelian (metabelian) level.
errors: (33) second line is written with '+' between (β_0 - σ(β_0)) and ω^{ν_2}σ; consistent with (36) and the next page it must be a product in the group, (β_0 - σβ_0)·ω^{ν_2}·σ.

The page only announces the verification of relation (34); as Grothendieck himself says on the next page, the computations are 'vaseux' logically. They implicitly take place in a larger free group, and rigor requires the intrinsic description (39) of 𝔊^+ as a pushout. That is a gap, but one he recognizes.
The commutativity/naturality of the group law on Σ̃ is asserted, not checked, on this page.

ideas.what: Parametrizing automorphisms of a fundamental-group-type extension by (odd scalar μ = 2ν+1, cocycle data α_0, β_0) subject to a 'loop equation' preserving inertia classes; action u(ρ) = ξρ, u(σ) = ω^{ν_2}η_0σ, with u acting by μ on the abelian kernel.
ideas.modern_name: Metabelian / abelianized truncation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (Drinfeld's GT parametrization (λ = 2m+1, f))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara (1980s-90s) for metabelian/pro-l Galois actions on π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points; Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps for genus-1 and modular variants
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic idea appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the explicit computations in La Longue Marche continuation are unpublished

ideas.what: Treating the parameter space of such automorphisms as a smooth group scheme over S_0 (refining a non-smooth, possibly disconnected in char 2,3 scheme Σ by passing to α, β coordinates).
ideas.modern_name: Group scheme of (metabelian) GT-type automorphisms / algebraic envelope
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pro-unipotent GT and related Deligne-style algebraic envelopes: Drinfeld, Deligne, Ihara (late 1980s-90s)

ideas.what: Using the 'relation des lacets' (preservation of inertia conjugacy classes) to force u(ε_0) = ε_0^{(μ)} and hence u = μ on M.
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic-character action on inertia / 'λ-power on inertia generators' condition

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly works out, scheme-theoretically over S_0 (including char 2, 3 subtleties), a smooth group scheme Σ̃_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms of a metabelian modular-type group 𝔊^+. Its parametrization (μ = 2ν+1 with ν = 2ν' + ν_2, plus cocycle data) is formally parallel to Drinfeld's GT parametrization a decade earlier. The smoothness and connectedness analysis in small characteristics seems not to have been pursued in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit le (schéma en groupes) Σ̃_{ρσ} muni d'une structure de groupe ..., et opérant sur 𝔊^+ via (33) u(ρ) = (α_0 - ρ(α_0) + ν_3λ_1)ρ, u(σ) = (β_0 - σ(β_0))ω^{ν_2}σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historically early, scheme-theoretic, metabelian GT-type object. Comparing it with Ihara's metabelian Galois representations and with integral/positive-characteristic versions of GT could be of interest, and it documents Grothendieck's own route toward GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification within a larger unpublished computation. Its interest is historical: an explicit, scheme-theoretic, metabelian GT-like parametrization with λ = 2m+1 parity bookkeeping, from before Drinfeld. Grothendieck's interest in such actions is known from the Esquisse, so it is only mildly surprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the group scheme is Σ̃_{ρσ} (the tilded Sigma of p. 40), not Z̃_{ρσ}; 'schéma en groupes' is struck and rewritten.
'structure de groupe commutatif' is more likely 'structure de groupe naturelle'.
(33) second line: the '+' is likely a slip; read (β_0 - σ(β_0))·ω^{ν_2}·σ.
'par la relation des locales' should be 'par la relation des lacets'.
Struck words before (35) read roughly 'en termes de ξ et η_0, [?]'.
